kind: Persistent reviewed reference knowledge, not weight training
rules: Plan the current script/delivery emotional arc first: funny, mock-serious, genuinely serious, reflective, energetic. Do not choose the same music merely because two scripts are both comedic.

Choose a timed section state before individual assets: voice only, music only, effects only, voice+music, voice+effects, full layered mix, intentional quiet. States may change within one video; no mandatory sound every second.
Assign each layer a distinct audible purpose: low weight, transient definition, tonal/emotional response, motion texture, space/decay or music. A pop+bell+tail trio is not a default for every word.

Vary timbre, rhythm, duration, register, intensity and layer roles, not just filenames. Repetition is justified only for a recurring story motif with development. Do not swap random sounds merely for novelty.

Use humorous stings/reactions only at actual punchlines; reserve serious tonal tension/low impacts for motivated moments. Never replace unavailable comic/serious material with an unrelated UI click, bird, horse or leaves.
Music entry, exit, passage, ducking, pause and return are compositional choices. A continuous bed is not compulsory. A music dropout is distinct from full digital silence.
Dense clusters belong around meaningful reveals/cuts/actions with complementary layers and offset starts; five starts in two seconds is not a per-window quota or proof of five simultaneous layers.

Anchor precise transients to a measured word/edit/action time. Sparse Vision observations describe setting only. Keep intentional tails across cuts where coherent; do not restart all layers on every cut.
References teach decisions, not a new rigid timestamp template. Apply their principles to new words, not their source timestamps, script, logo, watermarks or incidental objects.

The supplied three references are cinematic/automotive/editor-timeline examples, not verified comedy examples. Preserve the earlier E7/e2/e5 and owner comedy direction; do not invent humorous sounds as observations from these new samples.

CLAP similarity labels and Demucs residuals are approximate; do not call them exact isolated SFX, probabilities, layer counts or human listening. Automatic ASR found no reliable narration here. Local Qwen Vision cannot hear a video from its images alone.

Owner correction 25 October 2026: infer the actual subject, source activity and environment for each new video without waiting for owner sound-by-sound instructions. Prioritize supported scene sound layers before optional word ticks. A bike, water park, kitchen and indoor dialogue require different sound worlds.

Owner correction 25 October 2026: natural sound development controls duration, not spoken word length. Actual clicks can remain brief; joyful tonal stings, swells, sliding or resonant tails can last 1–3 seconds or longer. Sustain supported engines, surfaces and water ambience through the scene; do not stretch a short click or invent an unseen action.

Owner correction 25 October 2026: inspect across library folder labels when matching physical sound sources. A water recording may live in Foley or another folder; preserve subject checks and audio evaluation. Do not substitute a camera click, horse, bird or synthetic drone when a matching physical sound is unavailable.

Measured full-mix median drops from about -16 dB in the opening to -42 dB at 8–10.5s; late isolated activity returns. Composite audio resembles opening whooshes/low hits, a reverse swell around 4s, low decays and camera-like transients later. Identity unverified.

Dense staggered short clips sit over longer textures; timings do not reuse one ensemble at every shot. Approximate audio shifts from pulsing/rough rhythmic texture to a stronger low-impact ending at 6–8s. No verified separate engine/door source files.

reference_summaries.name: downloaded-video (2)
reference_summaries.summary: Cinematic SFX showcase with city/car/silhouette/subway shots, then waveform/title cards from about 17.5s. Relative quiet at 3.8–6.55s (-34.5 dB median), sustained string/score-like composite near 11–19s, stronger low-impact/pulse clusters around 20–24s and 26–28s, then decay. Exact layers and whether a tonal texture is music or designed SFX remain uncertain.
